title: Eight points with integer distances in general position
credit: Question posed by Kreisel and Kurz (2008), in the line of Erdos's question on integral point sets in general position
premise_risks: Could be resolved by a large computer search (it is a recognised open problem with refereed literature, but a positive answer might be pure computation)
Erdos's broader question is attributed to a person, but this specific 8-point question is unnamed
plain: Can you place eight points in the plane so that every pair is an integer distance apart, no three points lie on a line, and no four lie on a circle? Seven such points were found by computer in 2008. Nobody has found eight or shown that eight is impossible.
math: Decide whether there exist pairwise distinct $p_1,\dots,p_8\in\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $|p_i-p_j|\in\mathbb{Z}$ for all $i,j$, no three of the $p_i$ are collinear, and no four of the $p_i$ are concyclic.
